title.zh: 卷七十 列傳第三十 袁淑
title.raw: 卷七十 列傳第三十 袁淑 Volume 70 Biographies 30: Yuan Shu

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十 袁淑

translations.literal: Biographies 30: Yuan Shu
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 30: Yuan Shu

sentences.zh: 袁淑，字陽源，陳郡陽夏人，丹陽尹豹少子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery and the youngest son of Bao, Prefect of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery. He was the youngest son of Bao, who had served as Prefect of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少有風氣，年數歲，伯湛謂家人曰：「此非凡兒。

translations.literal: From youth he had spirit and bearing; when only a few years old, Bo Zhan said to the family: "This is no ordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed spirit and presence. When he was only a few years old, Bo Zhan told the household, "This is no ordinary child.

sentences.zh: 」至十餘歲，為姑夫王弘所賞。

translations.literal: " When he was more than ten, he won the admiration of Wang Hong, his uncle by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: " By his early teens he had won the admiration of Wang Hong, his uncle by marriage.

sentences.zh: 不為章句之學，而博涉多通，好屬文，辭采遒豔，縱橫有才辯。

translations.literal: He did not pursue the study of exegetical chapters, yet broadly mastered many fields; he loved literary composition—his phrasing was forceful and brilliant, and he had talent for eloquent disputation.
translations.idiomatic: He did not pursue the study of exegetical chapters, yet he mastered many fields through wide reading. He loved to write, and his prose was forceful and brilliant; he also had a gift for eloquent debate.

sentences.zh: 本州命主簿，著作佐郎，太子舍人，並不就。

translations.literal: The provincial authorities appointed him Registrar, Writing Assistant Gentleman, and Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Crown Prince; he accepted none of these posts.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial authorities appointed him Registrar, Writing Assistant Gentleman, and Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Crown Prince, but he accepted none of these posts.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康命為軍司祭酒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang, appointed him Libationer of the Army Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang, appointed him Libationer of the Army Office.

sentences.zh: 義康不好文學，雖外相禮接，意好甚疏。

translations.literal: Yikang did not care for literary studies; though outwardly he treated Shu with courtesy, inwardly his regard was very slight.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang cared little for literary studies. Though he treated Shu with outward courtesy, inwardly his regard was very slight.

sentences.zh: 劉湛，淑從母兄也，欲其附己，而淑不以為意，由是大相乖失，以久疾免官。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, Shu's maternal cousin, wanted Shu to attach himself to him, but Shu paid it no mind; thereby they fell greatly at odds, and Shu was dismissed on account of a long illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, Shu's maternal cousin, wanted Shu to attach himself to him, but Shu paid no heed. They fell sharply at odds, and Shu was dismissed on account of a long illness.

sentences.zh: 補衡陽王義季右軍主簿，遷太子洗馬，以腳疾不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Clerk to the Right Army of the Prince of Hengyang, Yiji, then promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent, but because of a foot ailment he did not take up the office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Senior Clerk to the Right Army of the Prince of Hengyang, Yiji, and was then promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent, but because of a foot ailment he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 衛軍臨川王義慶雅好文章，請為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: The Inspector-in-Chief of the Guard, the Prince of Linchuan, Yiqing, who greatly delighted in literature, invited him as Consulting Staff Member.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector-in-Chief of the Guard, the Prince of Linchuan, Yiqing, who greatly delighted in literature, invited him to serve as Consulting Staff Member.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Western Attendant of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Left Western Attendant of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 出為宣城太守，入補中書侍郎，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xuancheng, then entered to fill the post of Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Administrator of Xuancheng, then returned to the capital as Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, and left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 其秋，大舉北伐，淑侍坐從容曰：「今當鳴鑾中嶽，席捲趙、魏，檢玉岱宗，今其時也。

translations.literal: That autumn there was a great northern expedition; Shu, sitting in attendance, said with ease: "Now is the time to sound the imperial carriage at Mount Song, sweep through Zhao and Wei, and examine the jade at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the court launched a great northern expedition. Shu, sitting in attendance, said with easy confidence, "Now is the time to sound the imperial carriage at Mount Song, sweep through Zhao and Wei, and present jade at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 臣逢千載之會，願上《封禪書》一篇。

translations.literal: Your servant meets an age once in a thousand years and wishes to present a 'Treatise on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has met an age that comes once in a thousand years, and I wish to present a Treatise on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「盛德之事，我何足以當之。

translations.literal: " The Taizu laughed and said: "For a deed of vast virtue—I am not worthy to undertake it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Taizu laughed and said, "A deed of such vast virtue is more than I am worthy to undertake.

sentences.zh: 」出為始興王征北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: " He went out as Chief of Staff on the Northern Campaign Staff of the Prince of Shixing and Administrator of Eastern South Sea.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went out as Chief of Staff on the Northern Campaign Staff of the Prince of Shixing and as Administrator of Eastern South Sea.

sentences.zh: 淑始到府，浚引見，謂曰：「不意舅遂垂屈佐。

translations.literal: When Shu first arrived at the princely establishment, Jun summoned him for an audience and said: "I did not expect my uncle to condescend to serve as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu first arrived at the princely establishment, Jun summoned him for an audience and said, "I never expected my uncle to condescend to serve as my assistant.

sentences.zh: 」淑答曰：「朝廷遣下官，本以光公府望。

translations.literal: " Shu replied: "The court dispatched your humble servant precisely to lend brilliance to the prestige of your establishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu replied, "The court dispatched your humble servant precisely to lend brilliance to the prestige of your establishment.

sentences.zh: 」還為禦史中丞。

translations.literal: " He returned to serve as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He then returned to the capital to serve as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時索虜南侵，遂至瓜步，太祖使百官議防禦之術，淑上議曰：

translations.literal: At that time the barbarian Wei were invading south and had reached Guabu; the Taizu had the hundred officials discuss methods of defense; Shu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time the northern enemy invaded south as far as Guabu. The Taizu had the hundred officials discuss methods of defense, and Shu submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞函車之獸，離山必斃；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that beasts of the land in wheeled cages, once they leave the mountains, are bound to perish;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that beasts of the land, once caged and taken from the mountains, are bound to perish;

sentences.zh: 絕波之鱗，宕流則枯。

translations.literal: fish that break the waves, once the current is checked, wither.
translations.idiomatic: and fish that ride the waves, once the current is checked, wither away.

sentences.zh: 羯寇遺醜，趨致畿甸，蟻萃螽集，聞已崩殪。

translations.literal: The remnant villainy of the Jie raiders has rushed to the capital region; they gather like ants and swarm like locusts—I hear they are already collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant villainy of the Jie raiders has rushed into the capital region. They gather like ants and swarm like locusts, and I hear they are already near collapse.

sentences.zh: 天險岩曠，地限深遐，故全魏戢其圖，盛晉輟其議，情屈力殫，氣挫勇竭，諒不虞於來臨，本無怵於能濟矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's barriers are lofty and remote, the earth's limits deep and far—hence all Wei held back its designs, and flourishing Jin stayed its counsel; intent bent and strength spent, spirit blunted and courage exhausted—they surely did not anticipate a sudden coming, and from the first had no fear they could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's barriers are lofty and remote, and the earth's limits deep and far. Hence all Wei once held back its designs, and flourishing Jin stayed its counsel. Their intent was bent and their strength spent, their spirit blunted and their courage exhausted. They surely did not anticipate a sudden invasion, and from the first they had no fear that they could succeed.

sentences.zh: 乃者燮定攜遠，阻違授律，由將有弛拙，故士少鬥志。

translations.literal: Recently, in pacifying and settling the distant west, they defied our military law; because generals were lax or clumsy, the troops lacked fighting will.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, while pacifying and settling the distant west, they defied our military law. Because the generals were lax or clumsy, the troops lost their will to fight.

sentences.zh: 圍潰之眾，匪寇傾淪，攻制之師，空自班散，濟西勁騎，急戰蹴旅，淮上訓卒，簡備靡旗。

translations.literal: Besieged masses were not overthrown by the enemy's rush; strike forces vanished of their own accord in disarray; the fierce cavalry west of the Ji fled in hot battle; the trained soldiers on the Huai were picked clean and their banners went empty.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged masses were not overthrown by the enemy's rush, while strike forces scattered of their own accord. The fierce cavalry west of the Ji fled in hot battle, and the trained soldiers on the Huai were thinned until their banners stood empty.

sentences.zh: 是由綏整寡衷，戎昭多昧，遂使栲潞入患，泉伊來擾，紛殄姬風，泯毒禹績，騰書有渭陰之迫，懸烽均咸陽之警。

translations.literal: Thus harmony was maintained in few hearts, martial glory in much confusion; thereby the deep gorges brought calamity inland, springs and rivers brought disturbance—Ji culture was torn apart, Yu's legacy was poisoned; urgent dispatches pressed the land west of the Wei, beacon fires matched the alarms at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus harmony was kept in few hearts while martial glory was lost in much confusion. Deep gorges brought calamity inland, and springs and rivers brought disturbance. The culture of Ji was torn apart and the legacy of Yu was poisoned. Urgent dispatches pressed the land west of the Wei, and beacon fires matched the alarms at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 然而切揣虛實，伏匿先彰，校索伎能，譎詭既顯。

translations.literal: Yet probing carefully reality and pretense, hidden things were first revealed; examining means and skills, deceit was already exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once reality and pretense were carefully probed, what was hidden was first revealed; once means and skills were examined, deceit was already exposed.

sentences.zh: 綿地千里，彌行阻深，表裏躓硋，後先介逼。

translations.literal: A thousand li of territory, yet marching is blocked and deep; inside and outside they stumble and choke, rear and front hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: Though their territory spans a thousand li, every march is blocked and deep. Within and without they stumble and choke, and before and behind they are pressed on every side.

sentences.zh: 舍陵衍之習，競湍沙之利。

translations.literal: They abandon the habit of hill and plain and vie for the advantage of rushing sand.
translations.idiomatic: They have abandoned the habit of hill and plain and now vie for the advantage of rushing sand.

sentences.zh: 今虹見萍生，土膏泉動，津陸陷溢，痁禍洊興，芻稿已單，米粟莫系，水宇衿帶，進必傾殞，河隘扁固，退亦墮滅。

translations.literal: Now the rainbow appears and duckweed sprouts, the soil is moist and springs stir; roads and fords sink and overflow, pestilence arises again and again; fodder is already gone, grain cannot be tied up; the water realm girdles them—advancing they must topple and perish, the river barrier narrow and firm—retreating they likewise sink to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rainbow appears and duckweed sprouts, the soil turns moist and springs stir. Roads and fords sink and overflow, and pestilence rises again and again. Fodder is already gone and grain cannot be secured. The water realm girdles them: if they advance they must topple and perish; if they retreat, the narrow river barrier will likewise swallow them to destruction.

sentences.zh: 所謂棲烏於烈火之上，養魚于叢棘之中。

translations.literal: It is what people call roosting birds upon blazing fire and raising fish amid thorn thickets.
translations.idiomatic: This is what people call roosting birds upon blazing fire and raising fish amid thorn thickets.

sentences.zh: 或謂損緩江右，寬繕淮內。

translations.literal: Some say to lessen defenses on the Jiang's right and widen preparations within the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the court should lessen defenses on the Jiang's right and widen preparations within the Huai.

sentences.zh: 竊謂拯扼閩城，舊史為允，棄遠涼士，前言稱非。

translations.literal: I venture that holding fast to the Min region's frontier was approved in old histories; abandoning distant Liang warriors was denounced in earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: I venture that holding fast to the Min frontier was approved in old histories, while abandoning distant Liang warriors was denounced in earlier words.

sentences.zh: 限此要荒，猶弗委割。

translations.literal: Constrained to this vital wilderness, still they were not allowed to be surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Even when constrained to that vital wilderness, the court still did not allow it to be surrendered.

sentences.zh: 況聯被京國，咫尺神甸，數州摧掃，列邑殲痍，山淵反覆，草木塗地。

translations.literal: How much more when the capital itself is stricken, the sacred precinct within a stone's throw—how many prefectures have been swept bare, how many towns maimed; mountains and rivers overturned, vegetation painted with dead flesh.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when the capital itself is stricken and the sacred precinct lies within a stone's throw. How many prefectures have been swept bare and how many towns maimed! Mountains and rivers have overturned, and vegetation is painted with the flesh of the dead.

sentences.zh: 今丘賦千乘，井算萬集，肩摩倍于長安，締袂百於臨淄，什一而籍，實慊氓願，履畝以稅，既協農和。

translations.literal: Now the levy from households fills a thousand chariots, market tallies gather in ten thousands; shoulders rub closer than in Chang'an, gathered sleeves outnumber Linzi—the one-in-ten register truly satisfies the people's wish; taxing by the cultivated mu already suits the farmer's peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now the levy from households fills a thousand chariots, and market tallies gather in ten thousands. Shoulders rub closer than in Chang'an, and gathered sleeves outnumber Linzi. The one-in-ten register truly satisfies the people's wish, and taxing by the cultivated mu already suits the farmer's peace.

sentences.zh: 戶競戰心，人含銳志，皆欲贏糧請奮，釋緯乘城。

translations.literal: Every household competes in fighting spirit, every person holds a keen will—all wish to win grain and beg to charge, to throw off weaving and take the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Every household competes in fighting spirit, and every person holds a keen will. All wish to carry extra grain and beg to charge, to throw off weaving and man the walls.

sentences.zh: 謂宜懸金鑄印，要壯果之士，重幣甘辭，招摧決之將，舉薦板築之下，抽登臺皁之間，賞之以焚書，報之以相爵，俄而昭才賀闕，異能間至。

translations.literal: Say that gold should be hung and seals cast to summon stalwart fighters; heavy coin and sweet words to recruit men who will smash and decide; raise them from below the plasterer's scaffold, draw them from among the black-robed attendants on the tower—reward them with the burning of books, repay them with the prime minister's fief—and soon bright talent will fill the gate, unusual ability will arrive one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Hang gold and cast seals to summon stalwart fighters. Offer heavy coin and sweet words to recruit men who will smash the enemy and decide the day. Raise them from below the plasterer's scaffold and draw them from among the black-robed attendants on the tower. Reward them with the burning of books and repay them with the prime minister's fief, and soon bright talent will fill the gate and unusual ability will arrive one after another.

sentences.zh: 戎貪而無謀，肆而不整，迷乎向背之次，謬於合散之宜，犯軍志之極害，觸兵家之甚諱。

translations.literal: The barbarians are greedy and without stratagem, unrestrained and unformed; lost in the order of turning toward and away, mistaken in fitting union and dispersion—they have touched the utmost harm of military codes and the greatest taboo of the art of war.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners are greedy and without stratagem, unrestrained and unformed. Lost in the order of turning toward and away, mistaken in fitting union and dispersion, they have touched the utmost harm of military codes and the greatest taboo of the art of war.

sentences.zh: 鹹畜憤矣，僉策戰矣，稱願影從，謠言緡命。

translations.literal: All store up their wrath; all plan for battle; they call out wishing to follow like a shadow, ballads speak of pledging their lives.
translations.idiomatic: All store up their wrath and all plan for battle. They call out wishing to follow like a shadow, and ballads speak of pledging their lives.

sentences.zh: 宜選敢悍數千，騖行潛掩，偃旗裹甲，鉗馬銜枚，檜稽而起，晨壓未陣，旌噪亂舉，火鼓四臨，使景不暇移，塵不及起，無不禽鎩獸讋，冰解霧散，掃洗哨類，漂鹵浮山。

translations.literal: Choose several thousand bold and fierce, gallop in secret concealment, lower banners and wrap armor, bridled horses with gags in the mouth; rise at roll-call with the dawn pressing on their camp before they are formed—banners clamor and disorder breaks out, fires and drums close in on all sides—so that the foe has no time to shift his gaze, no time for dust to rise; none will fail to be captured and slaughtered like trembling beasts, melting like ice and dispersing like mist; sweep away the lookout bands, float the brine and flood the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Choose several thousand bold and fierce men, gallop in secret concealment, lower banners and wrap armor, and set bridled horses with gags in their mouths. Rise at roll-call and at dawn press on their camp before it is formed. Let banners clamor and disorder break out, and let fires and drums close in on all sides, so that the foe has no time to shift his gaze and no time for dust to rise. None will fail to be captured and slaughtered like trembling beasts, melting like ice and dispersing like mist. Sweep away the lookout bands and float the brine until it floods the hills.

sentences.zh: 如有決罦漏網，逡窠逗穴，命淮、汝戈船，遏其還徑，兗部勁卒，梗其歸塗。

translations.literal: Should any slip the net like a condemned criminal, linger in a nest or hide in a hole—order Huai and Ru boats with halberds to block their return road, and Yan Province's crack troops to choke their homeward path.
translations.idiomatic: Should any slip the net like a condemned criminal and linger in a nest or hide in a hole, order the Huai and Ru boats with halberds to block their return road, and Yan Province's crack troops to choke their homeward path.

sentences.zh: 必剪元雄，懸首麾下，乃將只輪不反，戰轊無旋矣。

translations.literal: You will surely cut down the chief villain and hang his head beneath your banners; then not a single wheel will return, not a war chariot will turn back.
translations.idiomatic: You will surely cut down the chief villain and hang his head beneath your banners. Then not a single wheel will return, and not a war chariot will turn back.

sentences.zh: 於是信臣騰威，武士繕力，緹組接陰，鞞柝聯響。

translations.literal: Thereupon loyal envoys will spread their prestige and warriors will tighten their strength; painted armor joins in shadow, watch-drums sound in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon loyal envoys will spread their prestige and warriors will tighten their strength. Painted armor will join in shadow, and watch-drums will sound in succession.

sentences.zh: 若其偽遁羸張，出沒無際，楚言漢旆，顯默如神，固已日月蔽虧，川穀蕩貿。

translations.literal: If they feign retreat and feign strength, appearing and vanishing without border—Chu speech and Han banners, manifest and hidden as spirits—already they veil sun and moon, shake valleys and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: If they feign retreat and feign strength, appearing and vanishing without border, with Chu speech and Han banners, manifest and hidden as spirits, already they veil sun and moon and shake valleys and rivers.

sentences.zh: 負塞殘孽，阻山燼黨，收險竊命，憑城借土，則當因威席捲，乘機芟剿。

translations.literal: As for remnant rebels holding passes, bandits blocking mountains—those who seize defiles and steal life, relying on walls and borrowed earth—then you should roll up your prestige and exploit the moment to mow them down.
translations.idiomatic: As for remnant rebels holding passes and bandits blocking mountains, those who seize defiles and steal life while relying on walls and borrowed earth, you should roll up your prestige and exploit the moment to mow them down.

sentences.zh: 泗、汴秀士，星流電燭，徐、阜嚴兵，雨湊雲集，蹶亂桑溪之北，搖潰浣海以南，絕其心根，勿使能植，銜索之枯，幾何不蠹。

translations.literal: The fine warriors of Si and Bian will stream like stars and flash like lightning; Yan and Fu will muster strict troops, gathering like rain and clouds—trampling disorder north of Sang Creek, rocking collapse south of Huan River—cutting off their heart-root so they cannot take hold again; withers bound by rope, how can they fail to rot?
translations.idiomatic: The fine warriors of Si and Bian will stream like stars and flash like lightning. Yan and Fu will muster strict troops, gathering like rain and clouds, trampling disorder north of Sang Creek and rocking collapse south of Huan River. Cut off their heart-root so they cannot take hold again. Withers bound by rope—how can they fail to rot?

sentences.zh: 是由涸澤而漁，焚林而狩，若浚風之亻舞輕籜，杲日之拂浮霜。

translations.literal: Thus is it like draining the marsh to fish and burning the forest to hunt—like a piercing wind shaking light bamboo slips, like bright sun brushing floating frost.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it will be like draining the marsh to fish and burning the forest to hunt, like a piercing wind shaking light bamboo slips, like bright sun brushing floating frost.

sentences.zh: 既而尉洽荷掠之餘，望吊網悲之鬼。

translations.literal: Then pacify those who remain from plunder among the lotuses, gaze in condolence upon ghosts netted in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Then pacify those who remain from plunder among the lotuses and gaze in condolence upon ghosts netted in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 然後天行樞運，猋舉煙升，青蓋西巡，翠華東幸，經啟州野，滌一軫策，俾高闕再勒，燕然後銘。

translations.literal: After that heaven moves the pivot of fate, tempest rises and smoke ascends—the blue canopy tours west, the emerald pennant journeys east—opening and cleansing the provinces and wilds, washing clean in one sweep of the whip—so that the high gate is inscribed again and Yanran marked afterward.
translations.idiomatic: After that heaven will move the pivot of fate, tempest will rise and smoke ascend. The blue canopy will tour west and the emerald pennant journey east, opening and cleansing the provinces and wilds and washing them clean in one sweep of the whip, so that the high gate is inscribed again and Yanran marked afterward.

sentences.zh: 方乃奠山沉河，創禮輯策，闡耀炎、昊之遺則，貫軼商、夏之舊文。

translations.literal: Only then sink the mountain and sink the river, create rites and compile records, radiate the surviving rules of Yan and Hao, thread through and surpass the old texts of Shang and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Only then will you sink offerings at the mountain and river, create rites and compile records, radiate the surviving rules of Yan and Hao, and thread through and surpass the old texts of Shang and Xia.

sentences.zh: 今眾賈拳勇，而將術疏怯，意者稔泰日積，承平歲久，邑無驚赴之急，家緩饋戰之勤，闕閱訓之禮，簡參屬之飾，且亦薦采之法，庸未蔇歟。

translations.literal: Now the masses possess martial valor, yet generals are lax and timid in method—may it be that long peace has accumulated day by day, years of undisturbed rule prolonged; no town has the urgency of answering alarm bells, no household the diligence of supplying war; the rites of drill and inspection are wanting, the ornaments of review and assignment are scant—and perhaps the method of recommended selection is not yet thorough?
translations.idiomatic: Now the masses possess martial valor, yet generals are lax and timid in method. May it be that long peace has accumulated day by day and years of undisturbed rule have grown prolonged, so that no town feels the urgency of answering alarm bells and no household keeps the diligence of supplying war. The rites of drill and inspection are wanting, and the ornaments of review and assignment are scant. Perhaps the method of recommended selection is not yet thorough?

sentences.zh: 若乃邦造裏選，攉論深切，躬擐盡幽，斬帶尋遠，設有沉明能照，俊偉自宣，誠感泉雨，流通金石，氣懾飛、賁，知窮苴、起，審邪正順逆之數，達昏明益損之宜，能睽合民心，愚睿物性，登丹墀而敷策，躡青蒲而揚謀，上說辰鑒，下弭素言，足以安民紓國，救災恤患。

translations.literal: If within the state's crafting, in village selection, one plumbs discourse to the depth, personally tests the utmost hidden, cuts the sash to seek the far—suppose there is one with profound clarity that shines, commanding talent that declares itself, sincerity that moves spring rains and flows through metal and stone, spirit that awes Fei and Ben, knowing that reaches Ju and Qi, discerning the numbers of wrong and right, bent and straight, understanding the fitting of obscurity and brightness, loss and gain, able to harmonize the people's hearts and know dull and sharp natures of things—ascend the red terrace and spread strategies, tread green rush and raise counsel above, persuading the celestial mirror below quieting plain words—enough to settle the people and ease the state, rescue disaster and pity the afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: If, within the state's crafting and in village selection, one plumbs discourse to the depth, personally tests the utmost hidden, and cuts the sash to seek the far, suppose there is one whose profound clarity shines forth and whose commanding talent declares itself, whose sincerity moves spring rains and flows through metal and stone, whose spirit awes Fei and Ben, whose knowing reaches Ju and Qi, who discerns the numbers of wrong and right, bent and straight, who understands the fitting of obscurity and brightness, loss and gain, who can harmonize the people's hearts and know the dull and sharp natures of things, who ascends the red terrace and spreads strategies and treads green rush to raise counsel above, persuading the celestial mirror and below quieting plain words—such a one would be enough to settle the people and ease the state, rescue disaster and pity the afflicted.

sentences.zh: 則宜拔過寵貴之上，褒升戚舊之右，別其旂章，榮其班祿，出得專譽，使不稟命。

translations.literal: Then he should be pulled above favored nobility, honored and promoted above kin of merit—given his own banner and insignia, glory in his rank and salary; going forth he may claim sole authority, orders need not be received.
translations.idiomatic: Then he should be pulled above favored nobility and honored and promoted above kin of merit. Give him his own banner and insignia and glory in rank and salary. Let him go forth with sole authority, without needing to receive orders.

sentences.zh: 降席折節，同廣武之請；

translations.literal: Lower his mat and bend his joint, as at Guangwu's request;
translations.idiomatic: Lower your mat and bend your joint, as at Guangwu's request;

sentences.zh: 設壇致禮，均淮陰之授。

translations.literal: raise an altar and perform rites, equal to bestowing command at Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: raise an altar and perform rites, equal to bestowing command at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 必有要盟之功，竊符之捷。

translations.literal: There will surely be the achievement of covenant oath, the success of stealing the tally.
translations.idiomatic: There will surely be the achievement of a covenant oath and the success of stealing the tally.

sentences.zh: 夷裔暴狠，內外侮棄，始附之眾，分茷無序，蠱以威利，勢必攜離，首順之徒，靡然自及。

translations.literal: The barbarian tribes are violent and cruel, deserted within and without; those first attached are without order in division; inflamed by authority and profit, they are bound to split apart; those who led the way will of themselves reach you.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian tribes are violent and cruel and deserted within and without. Those first attached are without order in division. Inflamed by authority and profit, they are bound to split apart, and those who led the way will of themselves come over to you.

sentences.zh: 今淶繹故典，瀍土纓緌，翦焉幽播，折首凶狡。

translations.literal: Now distill the old canons, rinse the soil and tether; shear and scatter the hidden, cut off the heads of the fierce and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Now distill the old canons, rinse the soil and tether, shear and scatter the hidden, and cut off the heads of the fierce and cunning.

sentences.zh: 是猶眇者願明，痿之思步，動商遄會，功終易感。

translations.literal: It is like the near-sighted longing for brightness, the lame longing to walk—when the merchant pitch sounds, achievement at last is easy to feel.
translations.idiomatic: It is like the near-sighted longing for brightness and the lame longing to walk: when the merchant pitch sounds, achievement at last is easy to feel.

sentences.zh: 劫晉在於善覘，全鄭實寄良諜，多縱反間，汨惑心耳，發險易之前，抵興喪之術，沖其猜伏，拂其嫌嗜，汨以連率之貴，餌以析壤之資。

translations.literal: Seizing Jin lay in keen observation; preserving Zheng truly rested on good spies—multiply wandering agents, muddy and confuse their hearts and ears; send before danger and easy, strike with arts of rise and fall; pierce their suspicions hidden, brush their dislikes cherished; muddy them with the honor of joint command, bait them with the asset of carved territory.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing Jin lay in keen observation, and preserving Zheng truly rested on good spies. Multiply wandering agents and muddy and confuse their hearts and ears. Send counsel before danger and ease, and strike with the arts of rise and fall. Pierce their hidden suspicions and brush their cherished dislikes. Muddy them with the honor of joint command and bait them with the asset of carved territory.

sentences.zh: 罄筆端之用，展辭鋒之銳，振辯則堅圍可解，馳羽而岩邑易傾。

translations.literal: Exhaust the uses of the brush tip, unfold the sharp edge of rhetoric—shake debate and solid walls can be opened, fly the letter and steep towns easily topple.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaust the uses of the brush tip and unfold the sharp edge of rhetoric. Shake debate and solid walls can be opened; fly the letter and steep towns easily topple.

sentences.zh: 必府鬲土崩，枝幹瓦裂，故燕、樂相悔，項、範交疑矣。

translations.literal: Surely the granary-like storehouse will crumble within, branches and trunks split like tiles—thus Yan and Yue regretted each other, Xiang and Fan came to mutual doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the granary-like storehouse will crumble within and branches and trunks will split like tiles. Thus Yan and Yue regretted each other, and Xiang and Fan came to mutual doubt.

sentences.zh: 或乃言約功深，事邇應廣，齊圉反駕，趙養還君，盡輿誦之道，畢能事之效。

translations.literal: Or again words few yet achievement deep, matter near yet response wide—Qi lord turned the carriage, Zhao nursed and returned the lord—entirely the way of street recitation, fully the effect of exhausting ability.
translations.idiomatic: Or again, though words be few the achievement is deep, though the matter be near the response is wide: the lord of Qi turned his carriage, and Zhao nursed and returned its lord. Entirely this is the way of street recitation and fully the effect of exhausting ability.

sentences.zh: 臣幸得出內層禁，遊心明代，澤與身泰，恩隨年行，無以逢迎昌運，潤飾鴻法。

translations.literal: Your servant is fortunate to have come from the inner layered prohibitions and to roam the heart in a bright age—favor has kept pace with the body, grace has moved with the years; he has no means to meet and welcome an auspicious fortune, to moisten and adorn the grand law.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is fortunate to have come from the inner layered prohibitions and to roam the heart in a bright age. Favor has kept pace with my body and grace has moved with the years, yet I have no means to meet and welcome an auspicious fortune or to moisten and adorn the grand law.

sentences.zh: 今塗有遺鏃，蠆未息蜂，敢思涼識，少酬閎施。

translations.literal: Now on the road are arrows left behind, scorpions and bees not yet stilled—I venture to bring forth modest views and repay a little the broad bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Now on the road lie arrows left behind, and scorpions and bees are not yet stilled. I venture to bring forth modest views and repay a little the broad bestowal.

sentences.zh: 但坐幕既乏昭文，免胄不能致果，竊觀都護之邊論，屬國之兵謨，終、晁之抗辭，杜、耿之言事，咸云及經之棘，猶闕上算，燭郛之敬，裁收下策。

translations.literal: Yet sitting in the tent there is lack of Zhao Wen, removing helm cannot bring result—I have observed the border discourse of the Chief Protector, the military stratagems of the Court of Dependencies, the resisting words of Zhong and Chao, the matter-speeches of Du and Geng—all say that reaching the thorn of the classics still lacks the upper calculation, and the respect of Zhu's outer wall barely adopts the lower stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet sitting in the tent there is lack of Zhao Wen, and removing the helm cannot bring result. I have observed the border discourse of the Chief Protector, the military stratagems of the Court of Dependencies, the resisting words of Zhong and Chao, and the policy speeches of Du and Geng. All say that reaching the thorn of the classics still lacks the upper calculation, and the respect shown at Zhu's outer wall barely adopts the lower stratagem.

sentences.zh: 自恥懦木，智不綜微，敢露昧見，無會昭采。

translations.literal: I myself am ashamed at timid wood, wisdom not weaving the minute—I venture to disclose a dark view, without meeting bright selection.
translations.idiomatic: I myself am ashamed at timid wood and wisdom that does not weave the minute. I venture to disclose a dark view, without meeting bright selection.

sentences.zh: 淑喜為誇誕，每為時人所嘲。

translations.literal: Shu delighted in grand and extravagant discourse and was often mocked by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Shu delighted in grand and extravagant discourse and was often mocked by men of the time.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗送錢三萬餉淑，一宿複遣追取，謂使人謬誤，欲以戲淑。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shixing, Jun, once sent thirty thousand cash to supply Shu; after one night he again sent to recover it, saying the messenger had erred and intending to tease Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shixing, Jun, once sent thirty thousand cash to supply Shu. After one night he sent again to recover it, saying the messenger had erred and intending to tease Shu.

sentences.zh: 淑與浚書曰：「袁司直之視館，敢寓書于上國之宮尹。

translations.literal: Shu wrote to Jun: "Yuan, Director of the Secretariat, viewing the lodging-house, ventures to lodge a letter with the palace steward of the upper state.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote to Jun, "Yuan, Director of the Secretariat, viewing the lodging-house, ventures to lodge a letter with the palace steward of the upper state.

sentences.zh: 日者猥枉泉賦，降委弊邑。

translations.literal: Recently you wrongly sent a spring levy, lowering it upon our poor district.
translations.idiomatic: Recently you wrongly sent a spring levy, lowering it upon our poor district.

sentences.zh: 弊邑敬事是遑，無或違貳。

translations.literal: Our poor district respectfully attends to the matter and dares not be double-minded.
translations.idiomatic: Our poor district respectfully attends to the matter and dares not be double-minded.

sentences.zh: 懼非郊贈之禮，覲饗之資，不虞君王惠之於是也，是有懵焉。

translations.literal: We fear it is not the gift of suburban presentation or the resource for audience and feast; we did not expect the king's grace in this, and therefore there is confusion.
translations.idiomatic: We fear it is not the gift of suburban presentation or the resource for audience and feast. We did not expect the king's grace in this, and therefore there is confusion.

sentences.zh: 弗圖旦夕發咫尺之記，籍左右而請，以為胥授失旨，爰速先幣。

translations.literal: We did not imagine that within the space of a day and night a note of a foot's breadth would issue, and through your attendants a request would be made, thinking the grant had missed its intent and therefore hastening the first gift.
translations.idiomatic: We did not imagine that within the space of a day and night a note of a foot's breadth would issue, and through your attendants a request would be made, thinking the grant had missed its intent and therefore hastening the first gift.

sentences.zh: 曾是附庸臣委末學孤聞者，如之何勿疑。

translations.literal: For a dependent minister and one of slight learning and lonely hearing such as I, how could there be doubt?
translations.idiomatic: For a dependent minister and one of slight learning and lonely hearing such as I, how could there be doubt?

sentences.zh: 且亦聞之前志曰，七年之中，一與一奪，義士猶或非之。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard in former records that within seven years, one grant and one withdrawal—even a man of righteousness might find fault.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have heard in former records that within seven years, one grant and one withdrawal—even a man of righteousness might find fault.

sentences.zh: 況密邇旬次，何其裒益之亟也。

translations.literal: How much more when it is close within a ten-day span—how sudden the increase and decrease!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when it is close within a ten-day span—how sudden the increase and decrease!

sentences.zh: 藉恐二三諸侯，有以觀大國之政。

translations.literal: I fear that the two or three feudal lords may thereby observe the government of the great state.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that the two or three feudal lords may thereby observe the government of the great state.

sentences.zh: 是用敢布心腹。

translations.literal: Therefore I venture to lay bare my inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I venture to lay bare my inmost heart.

sentences.zh: 弊室弱生，砥節清廉，好是潔直，以不邪之故，而貧聞天下。

translations.literal: My poor house and weak life polish the node and are pure and clean; I love what is pure and straight and, because I am not crooked, my poverty is known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: My poor house and weak life polish the node and are pure and clean. I love what is pure and straight, and because I am not crooked my poverty is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 甯有昧夫嗟金者哉。

translations.literal: Could there be one blind who sighs over gold?
translations.idiomatic: Could there be one blind who sighs over gold?

sentences.zh: 不腆供賦，束馬先璧以俟命。

translations.literal: Unworthily I supply the levy, bind horses and first present disks and await command.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthily I supply the levy, bind horses and first present disks, and await command.

sentences.zh: 唯執事所以圖之。」

translations.literal: Only let the steward take thought for it."
translations.idiomatic: Only let the steward take thought for it."

sentences.zh: 遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 元兇將為弑逆，其夜淑在直，二更許，呼淑及蕭斌等流涕謂曰：「主上信讒，將見罪廢。

translations.literal: The murderer was about to commit regicide; that night Shu was on night duty; at the second watch he summoned Shu and Xiao Bin and others, and with tears said: "The emperor trusts slander and is about to punish and depose me.
translations.idiomatic: The murderer was about to commit regicide. That night Shu was on night duty. At the second watch he summoned Shu and Xiao Bin and others and, weeping, said, "The emperor trusts slander and is about to punish and depose me.

sentences.zh: 內省無過，不能受枉。

translations.literal: Looking within, I have no fault and cannot accept wrongful ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Looking within, I have no fault and cannot accept wrongful ruin.

sentences.zh: 明旦便當行大事，望相與戮力。

translations.literal: Tomorrow morning I shall at once carry out the great affair; I hope you will join your strength with mine.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow morning I shall at once carry out the great affair. I hope you will join your strength with mine.

sentences.zh: 」淑及斌並曰：「自古無此，願加善思。

translations.literal: " Shu and Bin both said: "From antiquity there has never been this; I beg you to think more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu and Bin both said, "From antiquity there has never been this. I beg you to think more carefully.

sentences.zh: 」劭怒變色，左右皆動。

translations.literal: " Shao grew angry and changed color, and those at his side all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao grew angry and changed color, and those at his side all stirred.

sentences.zh: 斌懼，乃曰：「臣昔忝伏事，常思效節，況憂迫如此，輒當竭身奉令。

translations.literal: Bin was afraid and then said: "Your servant formerly served at your side and often thought to repay you with loyal effort; now that distress presses so close, I shall at once exhaust body and obey command.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was afraid and then said, "Your servant formerly served at your side and often thought to repay you with loyal effort. Now that distress presses so close, I shall at once exhaust my body and obey your command.

sentences.zh: 」淑叱之曰：「卿便謂殿下真有是邪？

translations.literal: " Shu rebuked him and said: "Do you then suppose His Highness truly means this?
translations.idiomatic: " Shu rebuked him and said, "Do you then suppose His Highness truly means this?

sentences.zh: 殿下幼時嘗患風，或是疾動耳。

translations.literal: His Highness in youth once suffered from wind; perhaps this is only the illness stirring.
translations.idiomatic: His Highness in youth once suffered from wind. Perhaps this is only the illness stirring.

sentences.zh: 」劭愈怒，因問曰：「事當克不？

translations.literal: " Shao grew still angrier and therefore asked: "Will the affair succeed or not?
translations.idiomatic: " Shao grew still angrier and therefore asked, "Will the affair succeed or not?

sentences.zh: 」淑曰：「居不疑之地，何患不克。

translations.literal: " Shu said: "Occupying a position free from doubt, what worry is there that it will not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: " Shu said, "Occupying a position free from doubt, what worry is there that it will not succeed?

sentences.zh: 但既克之後，為天地之所不容，大禍亦旋至耳。

translations.literal: But once it has succeeded, you will not be tolerated by heaven and earth, and great calamity will swiftly arrive.
translations.idiomatic: But once it has succeeded, you will not be tolerated by heaven and earth, and great calamity will swiftly arrive.

sentences.zh: 願急息之。

translations.literal: I beg you to abandon this at once.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to abandon this at once.

sentences.zh: 」劭左右引淑等袴褶，又就主衣取錦，截三尺為一段，又中破，分斌、淑及左右，使以縛袴。

translations.literal: " Shao's attendants pulled Shu and the others into trousers and jackets, then went to the chief wardrobe and took brocade, cut three feet into one section, split it again down the middle, and divided it among Bin, Shu, and the attendants to bind their trousers.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao's attendants pulled Shu and the others into trousers and jackets, then went to the chief wardrobe for brocade, cut three-foot lengths, split each in two, and gave pieces to Bin, Shu, and the attendants to bind their trousers.

sentences.zh: 淑出環省，繞床行，至四更乃寢。

translations.literal: Shu went out and walked around the hall, circling the bed; only at the fourth watch did he sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Shu went out and paced around the hall, circling the bed, and did not sleep until the fourth watch.

sentences.zh: 劭將出，已與蕭斌同載，呼淑甚急，淑眠終不起。

translations.literal: When Shao was about to go out, he was already in the same carriage as Xiao Bin; he called for Shu urgently, but Shu slept on and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao was about to set out, he was already in the carriage with Xiao Bin. He called urgently for Shu, but Shu slept on and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 劭停車奉化門，催之相續。

translations.literal: Shao stopped the carriage at Fenghua Gate and urged him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Shao halted the carriage at Fenghua Gate and urged him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 徐起至車後，劭使登車，又辭不上。

translations.literal: Shu slowly rose and came to the rear of the carriage; Shao had him mount, but he again declined and would not get in.
translations.idiomatic: Shu rose slowly and came to the rear of the carriage. Shao had him mount, but he again refused and would not board.

sentences.zh: 劭因命左右：「與手刃。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon ordered his attendants: "Give him a blade in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then ordered his attendants: "Cut him down yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」見殺於奉化門外，時年四十六。

translations.literal: " He was killed outside Fenghua Gate, at the age of forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: " He was killed outside Fenghua Gate at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 劭即位，追贈太常，賜賵甚厚。

translations.literal: When Shao took the throne, he posthumously honored him as Minister of Ceremonies and bestowed very generous funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao took the throne, he posthumously honored Shu as Minister of Ceremonies and bestowed lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 子幾、敳、棱、凝、標。

translations.literal: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.

sentences.zh: 敳，世祖步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Ai was Infantry Commandant under Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Ai served as Infantry Commandant under Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 凝，太宗世禦史中丞，出為晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Ning was Censor-in-Chief in the time of Emperor Taizong and went out as Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was Censor-in-Chief under Emperor Taizong and later went out as administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 太宗初與四方同反，兵敗歸降，以補劉湛冠軍府主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong's reign he rebelled with the four quarters, was defeated and surrendered, and was made Registrar of Liu Zhan's Staff of the General Who Vanquishes the Enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taizong's reign he joined the rebellion on all sides, was defeated and surrendered, and was appointed registrar on Liu Zhan's staff as General Who Vanquishes the Enemy.

sentences.zh: 淑諸子並早卒。

translations.literal: All of Shu's sons died young.
translations.idiomatic: All of Shu's sons died young.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：天長地久，人道則異於斯。

translations.literal: The historian says: Heaven is long and earth enduring, but the human way differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Heaven is long and earth enduring, yet the way of humanity is not like this.

sentences.zh: 蕣華朝露，未足以言也。

translations.literal: Hibiscus at morning dew is not enough to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Morning hibiscus and evening dew are hardly worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 其間夭遽，曾何足雲。

translations.literal: Among them, sudden early death—how could it be worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: Sudden early death among them—how could that even be worth mentioning?

sentences.zh: 宜任心去留，不以存沒嬰心。

translations.literal: One ought to let the heart go or stay as it will, and not bind the heart with survival or extinction.
translations.idiomatic: One ought to let the heart go or stay as it will, and not let life and death trouble the mind.

sentences.zh: 徒以靈化悠遠，生不再來，雖天行路險，而未之斯遇，謂七尺常存，百年可保也。

translations.literal: Only because spiritual transformation is remote and life does not come again—though heaven's road is perilous, one has not yet met it—one thinks the seven-foot body will always remain and a hundred years can be secured.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the spirit's transformation is far off and life does not return—though heaven's road is perilous, one has not yet met it—people think the seven-foot body will always remain and a hundred years can be secured.

sentences.zh: 所以據洪圖而輕天下，吝寸陰而敗尺璧。

translations.literal: Therefore they hold the great design lightly and treat the realm lightly, begrudge an inch of shadow and ruin a foot of jade.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they hold the great design lightly and treat the realm lightly, begrudge an inch of time and ruin a foot of jade.

sentences.zh: 若乃義重乎生，空炳前誥，投軀殉主，世罕其人。

translations.literal: If righteousness is heavier than life, it shines alone in earlier edicts; to cast away the body and die for one's lord is a man rarely seen in the age.
translations.idiomatic: When righteousness outweighs life, it shines alone in earlier edicts; to give one's body and die for one's lord is rare in any age.

sentences.zh: 若無陽源之節，丹青何貴焉爾！

translations.literal: Had there not been Yangyuan's integrity, how would scarlet and green be prized!
translations.idiomatic: Without Yangyuan's integrity, of what worth would the historian's brush be!
